chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from his father and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd al-Ashʿarī al-Qummī narrated to me, saying:
I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: How many rakʿahs is the salat (prayer)? He said: Fifty-one rakʿahs.

key_terms.إِحْدَى وَخَمْسُونَ: fifty-one, the total number stated in the narration
key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Riḍā, peace be upon him, the Imam being asked
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the salat (prayer), referring here to the total daily prescribed and recommended prayer units
key_terms.الْأَشْعَرِيُّ الْقُمِّيُّ: the Ashʿarī of Qum, identifying the narrator Ismāʿīl ibn Saʿd
key_terms.رَكْعَةٍ: a unit of prayer consisting of standing, bowing, and prostration

ai.seo_question: How many total rakʿahs are there in the daily salat (prayer) according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a question posed to al-Riḍā عليه السلام regarding the total number of rakʿahs in the daily salat (prayer). He answers that they are fifty-one rakʿahs, indicating the full count of the prescribed daily prayers together with their recommended units in the Shia tradition.
